claims.statement: The galasactl local init command creates the GALASA_HOME directory structure with essential configuration files including bootstrap.properties, galasactl.properties, cps.properties, credentials.properties, dss.properties, and overrides.properties
The galasactl local init --development flag configures the CLI to use snapshot Maven repositories and creates ${HOME}/.m2/settings.xml if it doesn't exist

The CLI uses three key environment variables: GALASA_HOME for configuration and test results directory (default ${HOME}/.galasa), GALASA_BOOTSTRAP for bootstrap file or URL location, and GALASA_TOKEN for personal access token authentication

The galasactl auth login command authenticates with a Galasa ecosystem using a personal access token and creates bearer-token.json in GALASA_HOME containing a JWT bearer token for subsequent API requests
The galasactl auth tokens get command lists all personal access tokens for the authenticated user, showing tokenid, creation date, expiry date, user, and description
The galasactl auth tokens delete command revokes a personal access token by token ID, preventing it from being used for authentication

The galasactl runs submit local command executes tests in a local JVM without ecosystem infrastructure, accepting parameters --obr for Maven coordinates of test bundles, --class for test class specification, and --log for log output

The galasactl runs submit local command supports --methods flag to run specific test methods within a class, with method names starting with letters, containing letters/numbers/underscores, and not being Java reserved keywords
The galasactl runs submit local command supports --gherkin flag to execute Gherkin feature files with a file URL ending in .feature extension
The galasactl runs submit local --offline flag prevents the JVM from contacting remote Maven repositories during bundle resolution, requiring all bundles to be present in the local Maven cache
The galasactl runs prepare local command pre-fetches all OSGi bundle dependencies for OBRs to the local Maven cache without running tests, preparing for offline test execution
The galasactl runs submit local command supports debug mode with --debug, --debugMode (listen or attach), and --debugPort parameters to enable Java debugger attachment

The galasactl runs submit command submits tests to a Galasa ecosystem for remote execution, with the run requestor set to the personal access token owner and optional --user flag to specify the associated user

The galasactl runs prepare command builds test portfolios from test streams with parameters --portfolio for output file, --stream for test stream, --package for test packages, --override for property overrides, and --append to add to existing portfolios
The galasactl runs get command retrieves information about test runs with --name parameter and --format option supporting summary, details, and raw output formats

The galasactl runs download command downloads all artifacts for a test run to a directory named after the run name, with --destination to specify custom location and --force to overwrite existing artifacts
The galasactl runs reset command resets a stuck or looping test in the ecosystem by requeuing it, with the server accepting the request asynchronously
The galasactl runs cancel command cancels a running test in the ecosystem while preserving RAS data already recorded, with the server accepting the request asynchronously
The galasactl runs delete command deletes a test run and all associated artifacts from the ecosystem's RAS

The galasactl runs cleanup local command executes resource management providers in a local JVM to clean up provisioned resources, accepting --obr for provider bundles, --includes-pattern and --excludes-pattern for glob-based provider selection
The galasactl properties get command retrieves properties from a namespace with filtering by --prefix, --infix, --suffix, or --name, and supports summary, raw, and yaml output formats
The galasactl properties set command creates or updates a property in a namespace using --name and --value parameters
The galasactl properties delete command removes a property from a namespace using the --name parameter
The galasactl properties namespaces get command lists all CPS namespaces with summary and raw output format support
The galasactl resources apply command creates or updates resources from a YAML file, creating resources that don't exist and updating those that do
The galasactl resources create command creates new resources from a YAML file, failing if resources already exist
The galasactl resources update command updates existing resources from a YAML file, failing if resources don't exist
The galasactl resources delete command removes resources defined in a YAML file from the ecosystem

The galasactl secrets get command retrieves secrets from the ecosystem's credentials store with optional --name parameter for specific secrets and --format parameter supporting summary and yaml output

The galasactl secrets set command creates or updates secrets with support for username/password/token combinations using --username, --password, --token flags and their base64-encoded variants --base64-username, --base64-password, --base64-token

The galasactl secrets set command supports keystore secrets (JKS or PKCS12) with --keystore-file for file path, --password for keystore password, --keystore-type for format, and --base64-keystore-encoded for pre-encoded data

The galasactl secrets set command supports opaque secrets for arbitrary binary data using --secret-file or --base64-secret, with a maximum raw file size of 760 KB that expands to approximately 1,013 KB when base64-encoded
The galasactl secrets set command supports changing secret types using the --type flag, requiring all credentials for the new type to be provided
The galasactl secrets delete command removes a secret from the credentials store using the --name parameter
The galasactl streams get command retrieves test streams from the Galasa service with optional --name parameter for specific streams and --format parameter supporting summary and yaml output
The galasactl streams set command creates or updates test streams with --name, --description, and --obr parameters
The galasactl streams delete command removes a test stream by name
The galasactl tags get command retrieves tags from the configuration property store with optional --name parameter and --format parameter supporting summary and yaml output
The galasactl tags set command creates or updates tags with --name, --description, and --priority parameters
The galasactl tags delete command removes a tag by name
The galasactl monitors get command retrieves resource cleanup monitors with optional --name parameter and --format parameter for different output formats
The galasactl monitors set command enables or disables monitors using --name and --is-enabled parameters
The galasactl users get command lists users in the ecosystem showing login-id, role, web-last-login, and rest-api-last-login, with optional --login-id parameter for specific users
The galasactl users set command allows administrators to change user roles with --login-id and --role parameters, and user priorities with --login-id and --priority parameters

The galasactl roles get command lists available roles in the ecosystem showing name and description, with optional --name and --format parameters, but roles are read-only and cannot be modified through the CLI

The galasactl project create command generates skeleton test projects with --package for package name, --features for multiple feature bundles, --obr to include OBR configuration, and build system options --maven and --gradle

The galasactl project create command supports --manager flag to create Galasa manager projects with optional --managerName, generating manager interfaces, implementations, resource interfaces, field handlers, exceptions, and unit tests

Local tests can use shared configuration from a remote Galasa ecosystem by setting framework.config.store=galasacps://<host>/api and framework.extra.bundles=dev.galasa.cps.rest in bootstrap.properties, requiring authentication with galasactl auth login

The CLI is available as pre-built binaries for darwin-x86_64, darwin-arm64, linux-x86_64, linux-s390x, and windows-x86_64 platforms from GitHub releases and as Docker images at ghcr.io/galasa-dev/galasactl-x86_64:main
The CLI implements exit code 0 for success and non-zero exit codes for failures, with machine-readable output formats (JSON/YAML) and non-interactive execution mode designed for CI/CD integration
